gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the U1's 5-second swap and the INDX's 12-second swap are measured differently. Prusa's ~12 s runs from the last extrusion on one tool to the first extrusion on the next, while Snapmaker's 5 s is an undefined 'typical' lab result. A hands-on reviewer timed the U1 at 10–12 s per colour change, which is about the same as the INDX, not 2.4× faster.
standout_why: 3dprinteray.com (cited) lists U1 '5-second swaps' and INDX 'about 12 s'. It says the two are not comparable because no common test is described, but it doesn't resolve the difference or give a measured figure. 3dtoolchangers.com/printers (cited) has no swap time or waste figure at all. ChatGPT's own answer repeats 'approximately 5-second tool swaps' for the U1 and gives no INDX time. Tom's Hardware best-picks (cited) would not open, so I couldn't check it. None of these pages gives Prusa's definition of its timing, a measured U1 swap time, or waste per swap on a common basis.
decides: It removes the U1's apparent speed edge over the INDX. Measured the same way, both swap in about 10–12 s, so the $749-vs-$1,999 choice comes down to enclosure and chamber heat (INDX up to 55 °C, U1 only an optional unheated Top Cover), waste per swap (INDX 0.013 g claimed with no prime tower, U1 about 0.049 g measured from its prime tower), and the INDX's smaller Y travel. Swap speed doesn't separate them. This confirms the U1 as the value pick but not as a faster one.

findings.label: Tool swap time, maker claim and its basis
findings.note: The page says it 'swaps one complete toolhead for another in just 5 seconds'. Footnote 1: 'This is a typical result from Snapmaker Lab tests and is for reference only.' It doesn't say where the timing starts or stops.

findings.label: Colour change time, measured by a reviewer
findings.source_title: Snapmaker U1 Review: An Affordable Tool Changer for Multicolor 3D Printing ⋆ stlDenise3D
findings.note: Denise Bertacchi, hands-on review, page last updated 2025-10-29. The parked head keeps its heater on standby and needs 'a quick prime' after a swap. That is 2–2.4× Snapmaker's 5 s claim and in the same range as Prusa's ~12 s INDX figure.

findings.label: Tool change time and how Prusa measures it
findings.source_title: INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One+ (Gen2) | Original Prusa 3D printers
findings.note: Prusa measures 'from the last extrusion on one material to the first extrusion on the next', on the model itself. This is the full time the print is interrupted, which is a stricter basis than Snapmaker's undefined 5 s. The printer page https://www.prusa3d.com/p/bondtech-indx lists 'About 12 seconds, about 0.013 g of waste' (read 2026-11-10).

findings.label: Waste per tool change, maker claim
findings.value: 0.013 g (13 mg) per change, no purge tower
findings.source_title: INDX 4-Tool Conversion Kit for CORE One+ (Gen2) | Original Prusa 3D printers
findings.note: Prusa claims this is '5× less than the most efficient systems and 30× less than standard filament rewinding systems' but gives no gram figure for those competitors. This is a maker claim, not an independent measurement.

findings.label: Prime-tower waste per swap, measured
findings.value: 4.4 g over 90 swaps ≈ 0.049 g per swap
findings.source_title: Snapmaker U1 Review: An Affordable Tool Changer for Multicolor 3D Printing ⋆ stlDenise3D
findings.note: Three-colour print with 90 swaps; 4.4 ÷ 90 = 0.049 g. That is about 3.8× Prusa's claimed 0.013 g per INDX change. The U1 figure is a measured prime tower and the INDX figure is Prusa's claim with no tower. The U1 tower varies with model height and slicer settings.

findings.label: Baseline behind the 'up to 85% less waste' claim
findings.value: up to 85% less filament than shared-nozzle filament-switching printers
findings.note: Footnote 4: 'Other' refers to a printer using shared-nozzle filament switching (an AMS-style setup). Footnote 5: total waste includes supports, the prime tower, pre-print nozzle clearing and flow calibration on the U1. So the U1 still prints a prime tower, while Prusa advertises 'No Purge-Tower' for the INDX.

findings.label: Build volume with INDX vs without
findings.value: 248 × 205 × 270 mm with INDX vs 250 × 220 × 270 mm without (−2 mm X, −15 mm Y)
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX | Multi-Material Toolchanger 3D Printer
findings.note: Both figures appear on the Prusa page; the subtraction is mine. The U1 page gives one figure, 270 × 270 × 270 mm, with no split for single tool vs all four tools.

findings.label: Max nozzle temp / chamber / US price
findings.value: 300 °C nozzle; chamber up to 55 °C; $1,999 (4-tool assembled), $2,249 (8-tool assembled), $1,699 / $1,949 kits
findings.source_title: Prusa CORE One+ (Gen 2) INDX | Multi-Material Toolchanger 3D Printer
findings.note: The tools are passive ('no motors, no heaters, no wires'). Heat comes from an induction coil on the moving head, so a 'tool' here is a nozzle and filament path. On the U1 and XL+ a tool is a complete toolhead.

findings.label: Swap time and waste, as Prusa states them
findings.value: no number: 'Tools are swapped in seconds'; 'virtually no purge waste'
findings.source_title: Prusa XL+ Single-Tool | Original Prusa 3D printers
findings.note: The page also gives 290 °C max nozzle; 360 × 360 × 360 mm; chamber up to 50 °C with the optional enclosure, 60 °C with an external heater marked 'Coming soon'. Single-tool price is $2,128.70; the 2- and 5-head prices didn't load.
